## Heritability and GWAS reveal different aspects of genetic architecture

Trait heritability poorly predicted genome-wide association mapping power. Starch, the most heritable nutritional trait, yielded only five loci, whereas protein, β-glucan and fiber, each with about half its heritability and near-identical to one another, yielded two, 11 and [TODO: Reminder for the user, NOT for the text: fiber was calibrated with the cultivated-barley NIR package only, with no wild-barley lab reference (Pintel MSc thesis, Table 1D), yet fiber is the trait with the most loci and two of the three presented genes. Decided 2026-09-26: no sentence or paragraph on this in the Discussion]{.comment-start id="404" author="TODO"}[[18]]{.mark}[]{.comment-end id="404"} loci, respectively. This contrast emphasizes that mapping success depends on components of the genetic architecture such as the number of alleles, their frequencies and effect sizes, and linkage disequilibrium, rather than on total genetic variation alone. For example, the fiber locus on chromosome 5H illustrates how a signal only just above the genome-wide threshold produced a strong separation between haplotypes once the markers across the glucanase gene were analyzed together. <!-- Added 2026-09-26 (user): the counterpart of the mini paper's 3H starch example (old_mini_paper/md/06_discussion.md, section 3), which cannot be reused (no "marginal" class any more; PHT4;3 has a mid-range lead and the weakest effect). src: fiber_L14 lead 5H:462,564,771, -log10(P) 6.0506 vs threshold 6.0454 = the weakest fiber lead (01_.../02_loci_FINAL/tables/Table_loci_master.tsv); GH17 5HG0487060 eta2 0.222, 1.41 SD, five groups, the largest effect of the three presented genes (05_.../08_USED_annotation_master/results/tables/Table_significant_genes_paper.tsv; Results Ch. 3). The comparison is on effect size, not P: the haplotype P (2.4e-05 raw) is not smaller than the GWAS lead P. --> <!-- src: loci per trait 01_.../02_loci_FINAL/tables/Table_loci_per_trait.tsv (starch 5, protein 2, beta-glucan 11, fiber 18); H2 Table 1 (00_THIN_.../outputs/subsection_1/tables/H2_GxE.csv: starch 0.474, fiber 0.248, protein 0.242, beta-glucan 0.234); rare leads 25 of 36 with MAF < 0.10 (Table_loci_master.tsv, Results Ch. 2) -->

Most associations rested on rare alleles, and at every fiber, β-glucan and starch locus the minor allele shifted grain composition in the direction of the phenotypic correlations, toward higher fiber and β-glucan and lower starch. This consistent direction requires closer attention. At most fiber and β-glucan loci, the minor-allele carriers originated mainly from [TODO: This inference rests on the dir-11 carrier-origin check (11_USED_check_low_maf_geographic_distribution_minor_allele), which is not in the Results. Decide whether to add its results (Online Resource + one M&M sentence) or keep the Discussion statement without them. Evidence: Desert is the top region of the minor-allele carriers at 22 of 29 fiber and beta-glucan leads against ~6 expected from matched genome-wide SNPs, and North at none; 81-94% of carriers exceed their own site-mates in the direction of the effect, and the carriers' sites predict only 17-33% of the carrier difference; the same Arad/Masada accessions carry the minor allele at many loci on different chromosomes; mean aIBS kinship between Desert sites 0.688 vs 0.664 between North sites (computed 2026-09-25 from 01_.../intermediates/morexV3_kinship.aIBS.kinf, read-only)]{.comment-start id="405" author="TODO"}[[desert and coast–desert sites]]{.mark}[]{.comment-end id="405"}, the populations that already produce low-starch, fiber- and β-glucan-rich grain. Such regional enrichment is expected if these alleles contributed to local adaptation, and does not by itself indicate an artefact. The carriers also came from several desert sites rather than a single one, and they differed from non-carriers of their own site in the direction of the allelic effect, supporting a genetic effect beyond geographic origin. However, the desert populations are closely related to one another, and correction for population structure is less effective for rare alleles shared by related accessions, so a contribution of common ancestry cannot be fully excluded. Plausible gene functions and phenotype-associated haplotypes further support individual loci, and the 7H locus, whose carriers were not concentrated in the desert, provides the clearest case.

Statistical rank was also a poor guide to biological candidacy. The most significant genes were often the least interpretable, unannotated or derived from mobile elements, whereas the genes with a clear route to the trait ranked lower. Because genes within a locus share one linkage-disequilibrium block, their significance largely reflects linkage with the lead signal rather than their own function, so significance identifies the locus, and biological relevance has to choose the gene. <!-- src: Results Ch. 3 (rank 1 6HG0619810 no functional call; rank 2 3HG0301210 transposase-derived); within fiber_L08 the two top-q genes are mobile-element-derived and within starch_L03 the top-q gene is a CRLK1-like kinase, not PHT4;3 (05_.../08_USED_annotation_master/TRAIT_CANDIDACY.md) -->

Two of the candidate genes connect to further evidence. The phosphate transporter suggests that plastid phosphate homeostasis contributes to the metabolic conditions required for starch accumulation, consistent with the impaired grain filling reported in rice phosphate-transporter mutants (Ma et al. 2021). The GDSL esterase/lipase at 7H suggests that the modification of cell-wall esters contributes to grain fiber, consistent with the roles of this family in arabinoxylan deacetylation and cutin deposition (Zhang et al. 2019; Girard et al. 2012). It cites the same references as Results Ch. 4 para 1 (Zhang et al. 2019; Girard et al. 2012), which are still to be verified under TODO 308. TODO 406 also noted a barley GDSL route through hull-caryopsis attachment with no citation found; it stays out of the text (section_materials/03_results/NOTE_7H_shared_signal_GDSL_gene.md). --> were confined to the putative promoter, while variants within the gene body showed no association, pointing to regulatory rather than coding variation. These four genes therefore identify distinct biological pathways for future investigation: cutin deposition, glucan hydrolysis, plastid phosphate transport and cell-wall ester modification. <!-- ref: Ma B, Zhang L, Gao Q et al (2021) A plasma membrane transporter coordinates phosphate reallocation and grain filling in cereals. Nat Genet 53:906-915 - in the mini paper's reference list (old_mini_paper/md/08_references.md line 51), reused as in the mini paper's Discussion. src: 7H promoter vs gene-body SNPs Results Ch. 4 (03_01_.../archive_v1_MGmin2_eps0.6/results/tables/local_association_profile.tsv). ## What the design can and cannot resolve

<!-- Round 2, drafted 2026-09-26 after the user approved sections 1-3. DISCUSSION_CANDIDATES items 4.2, 4.3, 4.6, 4.9 (4.8, the population-structure paragraph with TODO 407, drafted and removed by the user 2026-09-27) (4.1 "the locus, not the gene, is the unit of discovery" is already made at the end of the rank-vs-plausibility paragraph of section 3 and is not repeated here). Parameter values (r2 0.5, 50 kb gap rule, epsilon, MGmin) stay in M&M. -->

The genes carried forward passed two successive filters, and each of them can miss genuine candidates. The first, the definition of loci, delimits each association by linkage disequilibrium with its lead SNP and ends it at large gaps between SNPs, so the size of a locus is influenced by both the underlying genetic signal and the thresholds used to define it. A gene lying just outside a narrow locus is therefore never considered, as illustrated by the GDSL esterase/lipase at 7H, which lay beside two of the strongest signals of the study and was found only by examining the region directly. Accordingly, the absence of a candidate gene at a locus is weak evidence that none exists. The second filter, the haplotype analysis, requires sufficient variation within a gene to define haplotype groups, so a gene that could not be tested is not a gene without effect. Moreover, a single grouping setting was applied to all genes, and a setting suited to SNP-dense genes can fail to group the associated SNPs in sparse ones. The three genes carried forward are therefore those that passed both filters, not a complete list of the genes underlying these traits. <!-- src: locus definition (LD clumping with the lead, gap rule) 01_.../02_loci_FINAL/tables/locus_definition_params.tsv - values for M&M only; GDSL gene 554 bp beyond the starch locus, fiber and starch leads 7.25 and 6.44, the strongest of their traits (Results Ch. 4); untestable genes 25 of 55, all six protein genes (Results Ch. 3; 04_.../Stats/genes_not_tested.tsv). The "single grouping setting" sentence states the principle only; the 7H case (grouped only at a different setting) is M&M (BLUEPRINT Ch. 4, M&M hand-over) -->
